name: Pose set
markdown:
# Pose set

> From the author's earlier studio, cleaned for publication: private paths, ports and some lines were removed, so a step may read short and a screen it names may not exist here. Status in this studio: Untested.


## What it does
Takes THAT picture as the reference of an image-edit model and makes N (default 10) new pictures of the same person in the same setting, outfit, lighting and camera look, each in a
different pose. One grouped run: N ordinary studio jobs through `/api/studio/generate` in sequence (`queue_when_free`), resumable, cancellable, with a per-picture re-render. The
result is a contact sheet: the source first, then each pose with its check chips AND the reasons in words, Re-render, Keep, Download clean and Wipe + send.

## Step by step
1. Press **🧍 10 poses** on a finished image card (pick the picture when the card has several).
2. The form shows the plan: the detected framing and how, **what the scene was assumed to hold** (a phone?), the model, the time and VRAM estimate, any notes, and the list of poses.
3. Edit it: change a pose's words, remove a line, add a blank one or one from the bank, change how many (1-12), force the framing, pick the model. Changing an option redraws the list.
4. **Make N poses.** Watch the sheet. A picture whose check failed is re-rendered once with a new seed; if it fails again it says "needs your review": **Keep** it or **Re-render** it.

## The three ways to pose (the Model drop-down; each says its proof level)
| Pick | Entry | What it does | Per picture | Peak VRAM | Proof level |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Text instruction (Qwen-Image 2.1 edit)** (auto first) | `qwen21:edit` | primary: measured identity across the character sheet's pose / angle edits (ArcFace 0.751) | ~12 s | 36 GiB | recipe |
| **Text instruction (Klein 9B edit)** (auto fallback) | `img:klein_edit` | faster, weaker identity on the sheet (0.714, 2 weak of 9) | ~4 s (about 19 s all in on the author's live run) | 30 GiB | recipe |
| **Text instruction (Klein 9B + consistency LoRA)** | `img:klein_edit` + `f2k_9B_lcs_consist` 0.8 | the same, with the LoRA that cuts drift (MAD 43.5 against 58.7 in the KB test); its sentence follows the instruction (the library's placement rule for a fixed-sentence LoRA). Pulls toward the source: may under-change a pose. Never auto-picked until the proof run shows it helps | ~4.5 s | 30 GiB | load-tested (rendered once 2026-10-10, not judged) |
| Boogu Edit-Turbo | `img:boogu_edit` | fast preview; no character path | ~5 s | 31 GiB | recipe |
| FLUX.3 Klein edit | `flux3:edit` | only if you pick it and the lane is up; pose change is its known weak spot | ~6 s | 26 GiB | recipe |
The 4 GiB free-VRAM floor is kept by the tools' own preflight; with `queue_when_free` a short card waits instead of failing. The two LoRAs are never stacked: the model has one bypass slot and both model
pages make their own sentence the prompt.

## The instruction (raw, never enhanced)
`Same woman, same setting, same outfit and lighting. New pose: <pose>. Keep her face, hair, outfit and the background unchanged, and keep the camera angle and framing.` (woman / man /
person and her / his / their from the picture's prompt and the character's description). With a held phone: `She keeps holding the phone in the same hand as in the picture, and both arms stay visible.`
after the pose. A re-render after a failed ANATOMY check adds `Both arms, both hands and anything held in them must stay fully visible, with no missing or extra limbs.` Boogu: `Change the woman's pose
to <pose>. Keep her face, ... unchanged.` FLUX.3: the result is written with the reference as `<ref_image_0>`. The consistency route appends the library's own sentence. A saved character's identity-edit
lead is added by the studio as for any character edit. Every pose of a set uses the same words and the same seed (one seed family); a re-render or an automatic reroll moves it. **On Qwen the set seed is never 4242** (the seed that gives grainy Qwen edits, see [image-qwen21.md](image-qwen21.md)): no seed given = random, a requested 4242 is replaced by a per-run derived seed and the plan line says so; the per-picture seeds never land on it either. The other engines keep what was asked.

## The pose bank, the framing and the scene
(`data/image_deliverables/*.json`), so a reworded line there changes here; the rest are extensions. Each pose carries the least body the picture must show (`needs`: portrait <
waist < knee < full), the props the scene must already hold (`seat`, `wall`, `stairs`, `door`, `floor`, `phone`; looked for in the source's prompt), a family (standing, walking, seated,
leaning, floor, stairs, door, turn, hands, portrait, selfie) and three traits: `hands` (`both` = needs both hands free, `one` = needs a free hand), `expr` (mostly an expression / head change) and `hide` (the hands are
meant to be out of sight).
- **Framing** is detected from the picture (the face box height / picture height with the CPU face scorer: >= 0.30 head and shoulders, >= 0.17 waist up, >= 0.105 knees up, below that full
  body; first guesses), else from framing words in the prompt, else from the picture's shape (a guess, said so). A face crop is never asked for a full-body pose: only poses that fit are
  offered, and a plan line says how many were left out. Force the framing in the form when the detection is wrong.
- **Scene (a held phone / mirror selfie)**: a phone is found from the picture (DWPose + SigLIP2 on a crop around each hand) or the prompt's words (phone / selfie). Then poses that need both hands free are left
  out, the 10 **selfie** poses lead the set (one raised-phone body change each: three-quarter turn, phone low / high, shoulders away, peace sign / in the hair, leaning in, stepping
  back), the instruction keeps the phone and both arms, the pose-control skeletons raise the phone arm on the side the source holds it (flipped for the right hand), and the plan says what it assumed. Without a phone no
  selfie pose is offered.
- **Variety**: one pose per family per round in an order suited to the framing; **at most 2 (a set of 6 or fewer) or 3 expression-only poses per set**; poses whose props the scene lacks last (with a note); a seed
  only breaks ties. Fewer fitting poses than asked says so (and, when only expression poses are left, that the cap gave way).
- **Your list wins**: the poses you edit or add are used as written (a typed pose is read by the strict text guard too); a pose that needs both hands in a phone scene is kept but noted.

## Pose control: the skeletons
`pose_skeleton.py` draws an OpenPose / DWPose-style picture on the CPU (PIL, no model): 18 keypoints with the OpenPose colours and limb ellipses, a simple 21-point hand per wrist, on black, at the source's aspect (16 px
grid, about 1 MP, scaled again by the graph), placed so the head sits where the source's face box is and its size follows the box. The body is a small kinematic model in head-height units (bone lengths fixed,
foreshortening only shortens, body and head yaw, tilt for lying poses, hidden hands, a face point behind the head left out like OpenPose does); `pose_skeleton_table.py` has one spec per bank pose (107). Tests keep
it honest (bone lengths, symmetry, bounds, one distinct picture per pose, every bank pose has a spec); `scripts/pose_set_proof.py skeletons` writes the sheets to look at. How well the LoRA reads hand-drawn
skeletons is the open question of the proof run (the model page: trained on DWPose maps, works best when the map has the reference's proportions and scale; distilled works "with lower fidelity").

## Checks on each result (CPU, no GPU)
| Check | How | Fail / warn |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | ArcFace similarity of the result to the source picture (`facescore`) | fail < 0.50, warn < 0.60, warn when no face is found; skipped when the source has none. **A pose that turns the head 40 degrees or more (profile, a look away) only notes a match between 0.50 and 0.60** ("expected when the head turns this far") |
| Background unchanged | blurred colour difference outside both people (person box from the face box) | fail < 0.80, warn < 0.90; skipped when the person fills the frame |
| Pose different | difference inside the person box against the source, and against every other finished result | fail < 0.035 ("pose unchanged"), fail < 0.03 against another result ("near-identical to picture N") |
| **Grain** (Qwen only) | high-frequency energy of the result against the input picture (`studio/grain.py`): at least 2x AND at least 10 absolute is the grainy / over-sharpened Qwen failure (clean reads ~6, bad ~17.5, the input 4-6). The Qwen tool itself already re-renders a flagged result up to 2x with fresh seeds before the picture reaches this check (see [image-qwen21.md](image-qwen21.md)) | **fail** if it still flags, so the one automatic reroll runs with a NEW seed; the reason is on the picture |
| **Anatomy** | DWPose (the TorchScript pair the controlnet-aux pack keeps on disk) + SigLIP2 on a crop around each hand, CPU subprocess (`_anatomy_cli.py`): a hand the source shows must still be there (not for poses that hide or turn the hands), a held phone must stay, more people than the source warns | fail = a hand or the phone lost; a visible **"anatomy not checked"** when the estimator did not run (never a pass) |
First guesses (not calibrated; the proof run's `report` compares every reading with the verdicts). It cannot see missing fingers or an extra arm the estimator reads as one person. A fail triggers ONE automatic reroll
(after an anatomy fail its instruction says every limb and held thing stays visible); then `needs_review`. A re-render you ask for gets no automatic one. Checks flag; they never delete a picture. The contact sheet shows
every reason in words under the picture (what failed, what was only noted, what was not checked, what an earlier automatically re-rendered try said).

## Guards and gates (unchanged)
- Output guard on every result; the character stays bound on Qwen / Klein / pose control (face match to her sheet); Boogu is unbound (the identity check compares with the source).
- No Realism chip, persona or smart negative: edit engines go raw.

## Content Studio: the "pose set" item
A package item `{kind: 'poseset', source: {from_item: 'all' | 'iN' | from_template | job_ref}, count, engine, framing}` (the 🧍 Pose sets tab): one grouped pose-set run per picture set above it, made from that
set's FIRST finished picture (or one chosen finished picture), on the model you pick (auto = Qwen). The plan shows each set with its estimate (a labelled guess: the engine's per-picture time + the CPU checks), its
proof level and the checks; the 10 results are packaged with the other files, numbered and named `NN_Pose-set_k.png`, one post text per set, and each file goes through the same pre-post gate as a picture. A

## Proof (how a route becomes "verified")
(plan, minutes and VRAM in the research note section 6). `judge` composes one labelled sheet per case; `verdict` records per picture: pose changed? identity kept? outfit kept? background kept? anatomy ok? phone kept?
artefacts? -- tagged **orchestrator-visual** or **author**. A route passes when >= 7 of 10 are acceptable on >= 3 of the 4 plain sources and the mean face match is >= 0.65. **Only the author's verdicts can make a
level "verified"**; a visual review gives at most "judged by visual review, author to confirm". Until then the level in `readiness.json` (`edit.pose_set`, `klein_posectl`) stays **recipe** and the card says so.

## Runs, resume, cancel
State: `<guard state>/pose_sets/runs/ps<12 hex>.json` (`COMFY_POSESET_STATE` overrides), saved after every step; skeleton pictures under `.../skeletons/`. A saved "rendering" run with no live thread reads as interrupted after a
studio restart and **Resume** continues the pictures not done. **Cancel** cancels the running job. `POST /api/studio/poseset/runs/<id>/reroll {index}` and `/keep {index}`.

## Relation to other pages
- **Pictures** (`image-deliverables.md`): its pose-set templates make NEW pictures from text on a text-to-image model (one per line). This action EDITS an existing finished picture; the bank shares those lines.
- **Content Studio** (`content-studio.md`): the package item above; the Pictures templates remain a separate item kind.
- **Character sheet / Explore looks**: their body and angle shots are the measured evidence for the engine choice.

## Known limits
Qwen keeps the input's composition, so a pose that needs a different crop may under-change (flagged, rerolled once). Qwen-anchored sheets showed a glitter texture once; watch for it. Side
and back poses lower the face match. Prop poses assume the prop exists (the plan says when the prompt does not mention it). The drawn skeletons are plain stick figures with no depth cue. The
anatomy check reads hands and a held phone only. Not rendered and judged yet.

## Skeletons from a motion clip (2026-10-17)
The pose-control route's skeleton is drawn from a hand-made table. `studio/skeleton_from_motion.py` draws the same picture from a real motion frame (Kimodo, GEM-X, SAM 3D Body); the exact seams to let a pose name a motion frame instead of a bank pose are in [skeleton-from-motion.md](skeleton-from-motion.md). Not wired into the dialog.
